\chapter{Four More Forms Before Your Name}
\label{ch:gu-first-use-forms-b}
\hlchaptermodality{5}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read and write four more Gujarati consonants before they appear in the first name exchange: \gu{લ}, \gu{પ}, \gu{ચ}, and \gu{બ}.}

With every model covered, read \gu{લ}, \gu{પ}, \gu{ચ}, and \gu{બ} and write each one from a spoken sound cue, keeping reading and writing scores separate.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[la]{\gu{લ} — the consonant la}

\label{lesson:GU-W05-la}



\begin{quote}
Write retroflex \textbf{\gu{ળ}} once from memory. Say \emph{lla}, then put it away. The new letter is the ordinary \emph{l} sound.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{લ}} visible. It is \emph{la}. Circle counterclockwise around the broad rounded left body. Lift once and sweep the separate middle shoulder from left to right. Lift again; descend the tall right spine and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{લ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice rounded body, separate shoulder, separate spine; two pen lifts.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{લ}} once. Compare only the rounded body and separate shoulder; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{la} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{લ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Point to ordinary \emph{la} in \textbf{\gu{લ} \gu{ળ}}. Then point to retroflex \emph{lla}.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pa]{\gu{પ} — the consonant pa}

\label{lesson:GU-W05-pa}



\begin{quote}
Write \emph{la} once from memory. Check its rounded body; the next form begins with a high hook instead.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{પ}} visible. It is \emph{pa}. Begin at the high left hook, curl over it, descend the left stem, and sweep around the broad lower body into the right shoulder. Lift once; descend the tall right spine into its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{પ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice high left hook, broad lower body, separate right spine; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{પ}} once. Compare only the high hook and lower body; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{pa} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{પ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Name the first landmark and the pen-lift count.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cha]{\gu{ચ} — the consonant cha}

\label{lesson:GU-W05-cha}



\begin{quote}
Point to \textbf{\gu{છ}} and say aspirated \emph{chha} with its puff. The new \textbf{\gu{ચ}} is the shorter, unaspirated \emph{cha}: no extra puff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ચ}} visible. It is \emph{cha}. Circle the upper bowl, turn through the small middle loop, and continue around the broad lower body. Lift once; descend the separate right spine and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ચ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice upper bowl, small middle loop, broad lower body, separate spine; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ચ}} once. Compare only the upper bowl and middle loop; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write unaspirated \emph{cha} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ચ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\gu{ચ} \gu{છ}} aloud, keeping the second sound's puff.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ba]{\gu{બ} — the consonant ba}

\label{lesson:GU-W05-ba}



\begin{quote}
Write \emph{cha} once from memory. Check its small middle loop, then put that model away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{બ}} visible. It is \emph{ba}. Circle clockwise around the rounded left body, wind through the compact inner turn, and exit across the right shoulder. Lift once; descend the tall right spine and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{બ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice rounded outer body, compact inner turn, separate right spine; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{બ}} once. Compare only the outer body and inner turn; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ba} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{બ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Name the inner landmark and the pen-lift count.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la — pa — cha — ba]{\gu{લ} — \gu{પ} — \gu{ચ} — \gu{બ}: four more forms return}

\label{lesson:GU-R05-second-four-r1}



\begin{quote}
Keep the four cards visible. Point as you say \emph{la}, \emph{pa}, unaspirated \emph{cha}, and \emph{ba}. Notice one landmark at a time: rounded body, high hook, middle loop, compact inner turn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the row once from left to right. Record a reading score out of four.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Cover every model. Write \emph{la}, \emph{pa}, unaspirated \emph{cha}, and \emph{ba} from the four spoken cues. Record a separate writing score out of four. Aim for \textbf{4/4} in each column, with one focused repair allowed.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read \textbf{\gu{ક} \gu{ણ} \gu{શ}} once. Cover the row, then write \emph{ka}, retroflex \emph{nna}, and \emph{sha} from sound. Keep these older scores separate from the four-form chapter payoff; one repair is enough.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\gu{લ} \gu{ળ}} and \textbf{\gu{ચ} \gu{છ}} aloud. Keep ordinary/retroflex \emph{l} and unaspirated/aspirated \emph{ch} separate.
\end{tcolorbox}
